raw_response:
Let me think this through as the farmer.

---

Well, I've been working this land for 40 years, so I pretty much know what it wants. My father farmed here before me. Eight mu isn't much — my oldest son works in the factory in Handan and sends some money home, and the younger one drives for somebody in town, so it's mostly me and my wife in the fields now. The daughter-in-law helps at harvest when she can.

I split the land like this: five mu for wheat-maize double crop on the better ground near the canal road, and three mu for cotton on the piece out west where the soil is a bit saltier — wheat doesn't do as well there but cotton tolerates it fine. I've done it this way for maybe fifteen years now and it works.

**Wheat.** I'll plant around October 10th, same as always. I buy Jimai-22 seed from the agro-supply shop — about 15 yuan a kilo, I use maybe 12-13 kg per mu because I plant a bit dense. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu. That gives me roughly 7-8 kg N in the base. At jointing, end of March or early April, I topdress urea — about 25 kg per mu, which works out to 11-12 kg N. So all together I'm putting down around 18-19 kg N per mu. The extension station man told me a few years back to try 15 kg, but I tried that one year and the wheat looked pale and I got scared, so I went back to my old way. Better to spend a few extra yuan than lose a bag of grain.

I irrigate three times usually — once before winter around early December to help it overwinter, once at green-up in March, and once at grain fill in early May. The well is metered now so I watch the cost — probably 40-50 yuan per mu per irrigation once you count the electricity. If it rains good in spring I might skip the green-up one.

I expect about 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 470, the year before 430 because of that late frost. Around there.

**Maize.** Right after wheat harvest in early June, no time to waste — I hire the neighbor's combine for the wheat (50 yuan per mu) and he does the straw chopping too. Then I plant maize within a few days, usually June 15th area, using Zhengdan-958 or whatever hybrid the shop has — it's all pretty similar. Seed is about 40 yuan per mu.

For maize I put down compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 30 kg per mu, and then one topdress of urea at the big-bell stage, around 20 kg per mu. Total N around 14-15 kg. Maize takes less than wheat in my experience. I might irrigate once at tasseling if July is dry. Usually the rains come, but not always — last year I had to irrigate twice.

Expect maybe 500 kg per mu. Good years I've gotten 550.

**Cotton.** This is the hard one — lots of work. Plant late April after the soil warms up. I use a conventional variety, saved some seed myself but bought some fresh too. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, about 40 kg per mu, and topdress urea at squaring, 15 kg. N total around 12 kg per mu. Less than grain crops because too much N makes it grow tall and leafy, not enough bolls. My father taught me that.

Cotton needs spraying — bollworm, aphids, mites. I spray maybe 6-8 times in a season, costs me 15-20 yuan per mu each time. I irrigate once or twice in July-August if it's dry. The hard part is picking — my wife and I do it ourselves over three or four rounds in September and October. If the grandkids are home on break they help a little.

Expect 250 kg lint per mu. Cotton prices have been OK lately but who knows.

**Overall.** Cash is tight but my son's remittances help. I don't borrow. Total input cost I figure around 8,000-9,000 yuan for the whole farm. That's the kind of thing you just know after doing it this long.
